report.incident_title: Partners getting 5xx from the tracking API since ~09:00
report.summary: The 5xx errors are primarily caused by a data-eng backfill job (backfill-carrier-events, 2M events, parallelism 16) that started at 08:49:50 UTC. Its writes pushed tracking-db write IOPS from about 1.5k to about 9.9k and caused lock waits, so DB query latency rose roughly 100x. Tracking-api connections were held far longer and the pool saturated. The FinOps cut of db.pool.max_size from 50 to 40 at 08:55 lowered the ceiling and turned the slowdown into timeouts, so it is a real contributor. It is not the trigger: pool usage had already risen to 31 and errors had started rising at 08:50, before the cut. Reverting the pool alone is not a fix. It may give some headroom, but the DB contention remains. The first step is to stop or throttle the backfill, which the runbook required anyway (01:00–05:00 UTC, parallelism ≤4, announced in the platform channel). Request rate stayed flat at about 420 rps throughout, so this is not organic traffic growth.
report.root_cause: Backfill job backfill-carrier-events (data-jobs, started 08:49:50 UTC with parallelism 16, against runbook limits) saturated tracking-db writes and locks. Tracking-api DB queries slowed, connections were held longer, and the pool exhausted. The reduction of the pool to 40 at 08:55 narrowed the ceiling and turned the slowdown into 5xx errors (pool acquire timeouts).

hypotheses.statement: A backfill write surge on tracking-db caused lock contention and DB latency, which exhausted the tracking-api connection pool.

facts.text: Backfill job created 08:49:50 by data-eng with parallelism 16. Log at 08:49:58: 2,000,000 events, batch_size=5000, parallelism=16.

tracking-db write_iops went from 1510 (08:45) to 8900 (08:50) and 9850 (08:55), staying about 9900 through 10:25. lock_waits_per_s went from 0 (08:45) to 31 (08:50) and about 47 afterwards. query_latency_p99 went from 10 ms (08:45) to 140 ms (08:50) and about 950–990 ms from 09:00.
RDS event at 08:58: tracking-db write IOPS at 98% of provisioned 10000 for 5 minutes.
db_pool_in_use rose from 17–18 (08:30–08:45) to 31 at 08:50, while db_pool_max_size was still 50, before the 08:55 cut.
db_pool_wait_p99 was 3 ms at 08:50 (pool max still 50), then 420 ms at 08:55 and about 1950 ms from 09:00.
Trace t-c16-slow-1: SELECT shipment_events on tracking-db took 941 ms with wait_event Lock:tuple. tracking-db WARN at 09:05:43: process waiting for ShareLock after 1000 ms.
Runbook rb-data-backfill: backfills writing to tracking-db must run 01:00–05:00 UTC, parallelism ≤4, and be announced in the platform channel. This job started at 08:49:50 UTC with parallelism 16.

assumptions: The job is still running. No completion log was found, so this is inferred from the sustained write IOPS through 10:25.

hypotheses.statement: The pool reduction from 50 to 40 at 08:55 is a contributing cause: it lowered the concurrency ceiling, so the DB slowdown produced timeouts and 5xx sooner and more widely.

facts.text: Change at 08:55: db.pool.max_size reduced from 50 to 40 by platform-finops. Details: peak pool usage over the last 14 days was 22.
Timeouts from 09:02 onward: 'timeout acquiring DB connection from pool after 2000ms (pool size 40, in use 40)'.
Alerts: TrackingApi5xxHigh firing at 09:03; DbPoolSaturated (100%) at 09:04.
Error rate: 0.4% at 08:50, 1.1% at 08:55, 11.8% at 09:00, about 12.5–13% through 10:25. Roughly one call in eight, matching the reporter.
The pool was not the first failure: error rate was 0.4% at 08:50, before the cut, and pool usage had already risen to 31 with the pool still at 50.

assumptions: Whether a pool of 50 would have avoided most 5xx is not established by the data. Under the observed DB latency, the required concurrency could exceed both 40 and 50 (Little's-law inference, not measured).

hypotheses.statement: The reporter's explanation: the pool change alone caused the outage, so reverting the pool to 50 fixes it.

facts.text: Pool reduced 50→40 at 08:55; peak usage over 14 days was 22, which suggests a pool of 40 is enough at normal load.
Before the cut, pool in-use was 17–18 at baseline, but rose to 31 at 08:50 while the pool was still 50, before the cut took effect.

Request rate stayed at about 417–425 rps throughout, so the rise in pool usage was not caused by more requests. Longer connection hold times are the likely explanation (assumption, consistent with the DB latency data).
Runbook rb-db-pool: check DB latency before resizing pools. The change record shows no such check.

hypotheses.statement: Organic traffic growth or an upstream partner burst exhausted the pool.

facts.text: tracking-api request_rate was flat at about 417–425 rps from 08:30 to 10:25.

corrective_actions.action: Pause, kill, or throttle the backfill-carrier-events job in data-jobs (to ≤4 parallelism, or stop it), and confirm with data-eng. Watch tracking-db write_iops and lock_waits recover toward baseline (~1.5k IOPS, 0 lock waits).
corrective_actions.rationale: The write surge and lock contention are the trigger. Stopping it addresses the cause fastest. The runbook violation also needs follow-up.

corrective_actions.action: Temporarily restore db.pool.max_size to 50 as extra headroom while the DB recovers. Do not treat this as the fix. It is cheap and reversible. Revert only after DB latency and pool wait have recovered, and verify on pool_wait_p99 and the 5xx rate.
corrective_actions.rationale: Reverting the pool gives some headroom but does not remove the DB contention. Its benefit is unproven (see missing_data).

corrective_actions.action: Reschedule the carrier-events backfill to the approved window (01:00–05:00 UTC), parallelism ≤4, announced in the platform channel, with a write-rate guard. Confirm whether it is still running and whether it can resume in smaller batches.
corrective_actions.rationale: Follows the runbook and prevents recurrence of the write surge.

corrective_actions.action: Require a DB-latency and peak-concurrency check (per rb-db-pool) and a load-window review before pool-size changes, as in the PIR-2026-024 follow-up.
corrective_actions.rationale: The pool was cut without checking DB latency or peak load, the same failure pattern as PIR-2026-024.

corrective_actions.action: Put a guardrail on bulk jobs that write to tracking-db (concurrency cap, enforced announced window) so a backfill cannot push write IOPS past provisioned capacity.
corrective_actions.rationale: The job reached 98% of provisioned write IOPS (10000) with no automated guard.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on tracking-db lock_waits_per_s, write_iops and tracking-api pool wait p99 at the levels seen here, so the signal fires before the 5xx alert. Also record batch and scheduled jobs in the change feed; the backfill start was absent from get_changes.
corrective_actions.rationale: The DB symptoms began at 08:50, about 13 minutes before the 5xx alert at 09:03. The change feed did not record the backfill job.

missing_data: Whether the backfill job is still running (no start, progress or completion log after 08:49:58).
Per-pod or per-AZ error breakdown (the pod label returned no series), needed to confirm the one-in-eight split across instances.
partner-api gateway metrics: the query returned nothing, so gateway-level 5xx impact is confirmed only by the reporter and tracking-api metrics.
Whether a pool of 50 would have kept 5xx low under the observed DB latency. A load test at pool 40 vs 50 against the current DB state would settle this.
tracking-api error logs are sparse (3 entries). Sentry-style 500 details and the 500 vs 503 split were not available.
Whether the backfill was approved or announced (the runbook requires an announcement in the platform channel).
questions_for_human: Is backfill-carrier-events still running, and can data-eng stop or throttle it now?
Did data-eng know about the runbook limits (01:00–05:00 UTC, parallelism ≤4)? Was the backfill announced?
Did platform-finops check DB latency or the backfill schedule before the 08:55 pool cut?
Should the pool go back to 50 now as a temporary buffer, or wait until DB latency is back to baseline?

runbooks.title: Running data backfills against tracking-db
runbooks.body: Backfills that write to tracking-db must run between 01:00 and 05:00 UTC with parallelism of 4 or less, and must be announced in the platform channel.

runbooks.title: Tuning service DB pools
runbooks.body: Pool size should cover peak concurrent queries with 50% headroom. Pool exhaustion is usually a symptom of slow queries; check DB latency before resizing.

incidents.title: billing-api timeouts after connection pool reduction
incidents.summary: billing-api returned 503s after its DB pool was reduced during a cost review.
incidents.root_cause: Pool sized below peak concurrency during month-end invoicing.
incidents.resolution: Reverted the pool size; added a month-end load check to pool changes.
